final_answer: Ice floats on water because its molecular structure creates a less dense solid form compared to liquid water. In liquid water, molecules are in constant motion, moving closer and farther apart. When water freezes, hydrogen bonds between molecules form a stable, open hexagonal lattice. This structure creates more space between molecules than in liquid water, reducing its density. Since density determines buoyancy, ice’s lower density allows it to float on top of denser liquid water. This unique behavior is crucial for ecosystems, as it insulates bodies of water and sustains life beneath ice.
